name: Jindal Steel Ltd
title: Jindal Steel Ltd - 532286 - TRANSCRIPT OF EARNINGS CONFERENCE CALL HELD ON MAY 2, 2026

summary.headline: Jindal Steel Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,647 crores (INR 10,093/t) on ASP up INR 4,743/t QoQ, with FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery: consolidated gross revenue rose 28% QoQ to INR 19,399 crores and adjusted EBITDA reached INR 2,647 crores, helped by a rise in HRC and TMT rebar prices and Angul volume ramp-up. Sales volume grew 15% QoQ to 2.62 Mt as the Angul expansion took steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa. A one-time impairment of INR 1,433 crores (standalone) and INR 834 crores (consolidated) was booked on the Australian WCL asset after the shaft was closed. Management said the major capex programme is essentially complete and the focus shifts to asset sweating and deleveraging.

segments.name: Steel (India, Angul/Raigarh/Patratu)
segments.commentary: FY26 production 9.25 Mt (+14% YoY) and sales 8.68 Mt (+9% YoY). Q4 production 2.65 Mt (+6% QoQ, +26% YoY) and sales 2.62 Mt (+15% QoQ, +23% YoY). Flat/long mix was 52:48 in Q4 and 49:51 for FY26.

segments.name: Raw materials / overseas mines
segments.commentary: Iron ore sourcing about 60% outside purchases and 40% captive, with pricing described as stable. Mozambique is EBITDA positive, South Africa operating but not EBITDA positive, and Australia is closed with minimal cash burn.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: 1,050 MW Shree Bhoomi power plant commissioned (two 525 MW modules); ramp-up to complete within H1 FY27. Surplus power to be sold but described as not material to financials.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 11–11.5 Mt and sales at 10.5–11 Mt.
Q1 FY27 coking coal prices expected to rise by USD 20–25/t sequentially; iron ore movement of plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month.
Slurry pipeline (Barbil–Angul) to be commissioned in Q1 FY27; savings of about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps up.
Port facility to be commissioned; DRI-2 (2 Mtpa) expected towards end of FY27; PP2 also remaining.
Capex guidance of INR 7,500–10,000 crores for expansion and sustenance capex; remaining programme capex INR 11,545 crores.
Leverage expected to normalise by Q2 FY27; value-added flat mix expected to move from about 50% toward 70%.
Start-up costs of INR 125 crores in Q4 are said to be finished and not recurring.
capex_capacity: Steelmaking capacity raised to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa after BOF2 and BOF3 (3 Mt each) at Angul; iron-making capacity increased by 6.6 Mt through BF2 (4.6 Mt, operational) and DRI2 (2 Mt, under construction).
Cold rolling complex of 1.2 Mtpa commissioned at Angul to support value-added product mix.
Coal pipe conveyor from Utkal C thermal coal mine to Angul is operational; slurry pipeline from Barbil to Angul close to completion.
Total planned capex programme INR 47,043 crores: INR 25,924 crores spent up to FY25 and INR 9,574 crores in FY26, leaving INR 11,545 crores.
Thakurani-A1 iron ore block declared preferred bidder; Saradhapur Jalatap East coal block awarded at end of last year.
Rail rake programme of about 79 rakes: 72 acquired, remainder expected within 2–3 months.
demand_pricing: Management expects India steel demand growth of about 9–9.5% and cites FY26 finished steel consumption of 164.2 Mt (+8% YoY) and Q4 consumption of 44.6 Mt (+10% QoQ).

Realisations lag because the order book mixes spot and contract sales; contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations. Management said the market is holding firm despite a slight dip in recent weeks.
Management declined to give a Q1/Q2 realisation upside estimate, saying the market is hard to predict.
Flat sales focus is on infrastructure first, then building and construction, downstream products and automobiles. HSM grades developed for niche products are ramping in the current quarter.
Management said the Q4 sales run rate reflects seasonality, so no large sequential volume pickup is expected.
Safeguard duty on flat steel imports reduced to 11.5% from 12% effective 21 Apr 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will steel and realisation gains continue into Q1, and have contracts been reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts on earlier prices continue and ASP rose strongly in Q4 because of the spot/contract lag; the market is holding firm, though slightly softer recently.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company shift to asset sweating rather than further capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the capex programme is essentially complete and the focus is on sweating assets, with INR 7,500–10,000 crores allocated to expansion and sustenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why is value-added share falling and what is the target mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the priority during ramp-up is utilisation, with mix optimisation starting in H1 FY27 and stabilising in H2. Flat mix is about 50:50 today and is expected to reach about 70% flat over time.

qa_highlights.question: What were the start-up costs this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q4 start-up costs at INR 125 crores, most of which were booked in Q3, and said these will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the slurry pipeline savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slurry savings are about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps. Full utilisation is not expected this year, but per-tonne savings do not depend on utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further write-downs on overseas assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no further write-downs are expected, based on an independent valuation. Australia has minimal cash outflow, and Mozambique is EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: What are the raw material cost moves into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal is expected to rise USD 20–25/t QoQ in Q1. Iron ore is expected to move by about plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month and is hard to predict.

risks_watch: Value-added product share fell to about 61% from 66% QoQ, and management says mix will move back toward normal levels only over time.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20–25/t in Q1 FY27 could compress margins if steel prices soften; a dip in steel prices was acknowledged.
FY26 EBITDA per tonne fell to INR 10,482 from INR 11,712 in FY25 even as volume rose.
DRI-2 is due towards end FY27 and PP2 is also pending; slurry pipeline commissioning is due in Q1 FY27.
Leverage (1.66x net debt/EBITDA) is expected to normalise only by Q2 FY27.
Management gave no EBITDA margin or revenue guidance for FY27, only volume guidance.
Overseas mine EC capacity increase is pending with no date given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, demand and the end of the capex cycle, with management repeatedly calling the market healthy. Evasive on pricing, margins, revenue and the timing of DRI-2 and raw material moves, and it referred several questions to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Our focus is on sweating the assets and getting returns out of them.
I think you are going to see a little bit of movement in the first two quarters of this year and then a stabilization in the second half of the year.
It is a cost. Cost cannot be reversed.

adds.what: BOF2 and BOF3 steelmaking units (3 Mt each) at Angul, raising steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa
BF2 blast furnace (4.6 Mt iron-making) operational
1.2 Mtpa cold rolling complex at Angul
DRI-2 direct reduced iron plant (2 Mtpa), expected towards end of FY27

growth.why: FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt and production at 11–11.5 Mt, with BOF2/BOF3 and BF2 already live and Q4 sales up 15% QoQ, though management said Q4 run-rate reflects seasonality and no large volume pickup is expected; the call says the major capex programme is essentially complete, so growth rests on ramp-up, mix and pricing rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Slurry pipeline savings of INR 750–1,000/t of steel from Q1 FY27 and start-up costs (INR 125 crore in Q4) not recurring support margins, offset by coking coal up USD 20–25/t and FY26 EBITDA/t down to INR 10,482 from INR 11,712.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Major capex programme 'essentially complete' with BOF2/BOF3 (3 Mt each) and BF2 already live, taking steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa; only DRI-2 (2 Mtpa) under construction for towards end FY27, which falls at the edge of the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt vs FY26 sales of 8.68 Mt (+21–27%), with BOF2/BOF3 live and production guided at 11–11.5 Mt; but management said Q4 run-rate reflects seasonality and no large sequential pickup is expected.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said focus is on sweating assets with INR 7,500–10,000 crore allocated to expansion and sustenance capex against INR 11,545 crore remaining programme; no new greenfield capex signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 ASP rose INR 4,743/t QoQ and contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations, but management declined to give any realisation upside estimate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coking coal expected up USD 20–25/t QoQ in Q1 FY27 and steel prices showed a slight dip in recent weeks, so margin compression is possible; no EBITDA guidance was given to measure against.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: HSM grades for niche products are ramping in the current quarter and flat mix is to move from about 50% toward 70% over time, though no specific product dates were given.

rows.label: Leverage normalises by Q2 FY27
rows.why: Net debt INR 16,019 crore at 1.66x net debt/EBITDA and D/E 0.43x; management guided normalisation by Q2 FY27 as capex winds down.

rows.label: Slurry pipeline commissioning
rows.why: Barbil–Angul slurry pipeline to save about INR 700/t of iron ore (INR 750–1,000/t of steel) as it ramps, with savings not dependent on utilisation.

rows.label: Contract prices lag spot
rows.why: Order book mixes spot and contract sales; contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations, but market dipped slightly in recent weeks.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, demand (9–9.5% growth) and the end of the capex cycle, but cautious and evasive on realisations, margins, coking coal and iron ore moves, and DRI-2 timing; analysts pushed on pricing, write-downs and mix.
